sanskrit: rudrāṇī tu tataḥ kruddhā prajocchede tathā kṛte devān athābravīt tatra strībhāvāt paruṣaṃ vacaḥ
english: Then Rudrāṇī, enraged that the begetting of offspring had thus been cut off, spoke to the gods, in her womanly nature, harsh words.

sanskrit: yasmād apatyakāmo vai bhartā me vinivartitaḥ tasmāt sarve surā yūyam anapatyā bhaviṣyatha
english: "Because my husband, who longed for offspring, has been turned from his purpose, therefore all of you gods shall be without progeny.

sanskrit: prajocchedo mama kṛto yasmād yuṣmābhir adya vai tasmāt prajā vaḥ khagamāḥ sarveṣāṃ na bhaviṣyati
english: Since the cutting off of my offspring has been wrought by you this day, therefore, O sky-rangers, none of you shall have progeny."

sanskrit: pāvakas tu na tatrāsīc chāpakāle bhṛgūdvaha devā devyās tathā śāpād anapatyās tadābhavan
english: But Pāvaka was not present there at the time of the curse, O scion of Bhṛgu; and so, by the goddess's curse, the gods became without offspring.

sanskrit: rudras tu tejo 'pratimaṃ dhārayām āsa tat tadā praskannaṃ tu tatas tasmāt kiṃ cit tatrāpatad bhuvi
english: Rudra, meanwhile, held back that incomparable seed; yet something of it spilled forth from him and fell there upon the earth.

sanskrit: tat papāta tadā cāgnau vavṛdhe cādbhutopamam tejas tejasi saṃpṛktam ekayonitvam āgatam
english: That fell then into the fire and grew, a thing of wondrous likeness; radiance mingled with radiance, and so came to share a single source.

sanskrit: etasminn eva kāle tu devāḥ śakrapurogamāḥ asuras tārako nāma tena saṃtāpitā bhṛśam
english: At this very time the gods, with Śakra at their head, were grievously tormented by an asura named Tāraka.

sanskrit: ādityā vasavo rudrā maruto 'thāśvināv api sādhyāś ca sarve saṃtrastā daiteyasya parākramāt
english: The Ādityas, the Vasus, the Rudras, the Maruts, and the two Aśvins, and all the Sādhyas, were terrified by the prowess of that descendant of Diti.

sanskrit: sthānāni devatānāṃ hi vimānāni purāṇi ca ṛṣīṇām āśramāś caiva babhūvur asurair hṛtāḥ
english: For the abodes of the gods, their celestial chariots and cities, and the hermitages of the sages too were seized by the asuras.

sanskrit: te dīnamanasaḥ sarve devāś ca ṛṣayaś ca ha prajagmuḥ śaraṇaṃ devaṃ brahmāṇam ajaraṃ prabhum
english: All of them, downcast in heart—the gods and the sages alike—went for refuge to the god Brahmā, the undecaying lord.

sanskrit: devā ūcuḥ asuras tārako nāma tvayā dattavaraḥ prabho surān ṛṣīṃś ca kliśnāti vadhas tasya vidhīyatām
english: The gods said: "An asura named Tāraka, to whom you granted a boon, O Lord, afflicts the gods and the sages; let his slaying be ordained.

sanskrit: tasmād bhayaṃ samutpannam asmākaṃ vai pitāmaha paritrāyasva no deva na hy anyā gatir asti naḥ
english: From him terror has arisen for us, O Grandsire; save us, O god, for we have no other refuge."

sanskrit: brahmovāca samo 'haṃ sarvabhūtānām adharmaṃ neha rocaye hanyatāṃ tārakaḥ kṣipraṃ surarṣigaṇabādhakaḥ
english: Brahmā said: "I am equal toward all beings, and I take no pleasure in unrighteousness; let Tāraka, the oppressor of the hosts of gods and sages, be slain swiftly.

sanskrit: vedā dharmāś ca notsādaṃ gaccheyuḥ surasattamāḥ vihitaṃ pūrvam evātra mayā vai vyetu vo jvaraḥ
english: The Vedas and the laws of dharma must not go to ruin, O best of gods; this matter has already been provided for by me—let your fever pass away.

sanskrit: devā ūcuḥ varadānād bhagavato daiteyo balagarvitaḥ devair na śakyate hantuṃ sa kathaṃ praśamaṃ vrajet
english: The gods said: "By the granting of your boon, O blessed one, the son of Diti is proud of his strength; he cannot be slain by the gods—how then shall he be brought to an end?

sanskrit: sa hi naiva sma devānāṃ nāsurāṇāṃ na rakṣasām vadhyaḥ syām iti jagrāha varaṃ tvattaḥ pitāmaha
english: For he obtained from you, O Grandsire, the boon: 'May I be slayable neither by the gods, nor by the asuras, nor by the rākṣasas.'

sanskrit: devāś ca śaptā rudrāṇyā prajocchede purā kṛte na bhaviṣyati vo 'patyam iti sarvajagatpate
english: And the gods were cursed by Rudrāṇī, when the cutting off of her offspring was wrought of old: 'You shall have no progeny,' O lord of all the worlds."

sanskrit: brahmovāca hutāśano na tatrāsīc chāpakāle surottamāḥ sa utpādayitāpatyaṃ vadhārthaṃ tridaśadviṣām
english: Brahmā said: "Hutāśana was not present there at the time of the curse, O best of gods; he shall beget offspring for the slaying of the foes of the Thirty.

sanskrit: tad vai sarvān atikramya devadānavarākṣasān mānuṣān atha gandharvān nāgān atha ca pakṣiṇaḥ
english: That offspring, surpassing all—gods, dānavas, and rākṣasas, men and gandharvas, nāgas and birds—

sanskrit: astreṇāmoghapātena śaktyā taṃ ghātayiṣyati yato vo bhayam utpannaṃ ye cānye suraśatravaḥ
english: with a weapon of unfailing aim, with his spear, shall slay him from whom your terror has arisen, and whatever other foes of the gods there be.

sanskrit: sanātano hi saṃkalpaḥ kāma ity abhidhīyate rudrasya tejaḥ praskannam agnau nipatitaṃ ca tat
english: For the eternal Resolve is named Kāma; and the seed of Rudra spilled forth and fell into the fire.

sanskrit: tat tejo 'gnir mahad bhūtaṃ dvitīyam iva pāvakam vadhārthaṃ devaśatrūṇāṃ gaṅgāyāṃ janayiṣyati
english: That radiance, become a mighty being, like a second Fire, Agni shall bring to birth in the Gaṅgā for the slaying of the foes of the gods.

sanskrit: sa tu nāvāpa taṃ śāpaṃ naṣṭaḥ sa hutabhuk tadā tasmād vo bhayahṛd devāḥ samutpatsyati pāvakiḥ
english: He, the eater of oblations, did not incur that curse, for he had vanished at the time; therefore, O gods, the son of Pāvaka shall arise as the remover of your fear.

sanskrit: anviṣyatāṃ vai jvalanas tathā cādya niyujyatām tārakasya vadhopāyaḥ kathito vai mayānaghāḥ
english: Let the Burning One be sought out, then, and appointed this day to the task; the means of Tāraka's slaying has been told you by me, O sinless ones.

sanskrit: na hi tejasvināṃ śāpās tejaḥsu prabhavanti vai balāny atibalaṃ prāpya nabalāni bhavanti vai
english: For curses do not prevail over the radiance of the radiant; lesser powers, when they meet a greater power, become powerless indeed.

sanskrit: hanyād avadhyān varadān api caiva tapasvinaḥ saṃkalpābhiruciḥ kāmaḥ sanātanatamo 'nalaḥ
english: Kāma, who is delight in resolve, the most ancient Fire, could slay even the unslayable, the granters of boons, and the ascetics.

sanskrit: jagatpatir anirdeśyaḥ sarvagaḥ sarvabhāvanaḥ hṛcchayaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ jyeṣṭho rudrād api prabhuḥ
english: He is the lord of the world, indefinable, all-pervading, the source of all being, the one who dwells in the hearts of all creatures, the eldest, a lord mightier even than Rudra.

sanskrit: anviṣyatāṃ sa tu kṣipraṃ tejorāśir hutāśanaḥ sa vo manogataṃ kāmaṃ devaḥ saṃpādayiṣyati
english: Let him be sought out swiftly, Hutāśana, that mass of radiance; that god shall fulfill the desire that lies in your hearts."

sanskrit: etad vākyam upaśrutya tato devā mahātmanaḥ jagmuḥ saṃsiddhasaṃkalpāḥ paryeṣanto vibhāvasum
english: Having heard this speech of the great-souled one, the gods then went forth, their resolve made firm, searching for Vibhāvasu.

sanskrit: tatas trailokyam ṛṣayo vyacinvanta suraiḥ saha kāṅkṣanto darśanaṃ vahneḥ sarve tadgatamānasāḥ
english: Then the sages, together with the gods, searched through the three worlds, longing for the sight of Vahni, all with their minds fixed upon him.

sanskrit: pareṇa tapasā yuktāḥ śrīmanto lokaviśrutāḥ lokān anvacaran siddhāḥ sarva eva bhṛgūdvaha naṣṭam ātmani saṃlīnaṃ nādhijagmur hutāśanam
english: Endowed with the highest austerity, glorious, renowned throughout the worlds, the perfected ones all ranged across the worlds, O scion of Bhṛgu; yet they did not find Hutāśana, who had vanished, withdrawn into himself.

sanskrit: tataḥ saṃjātasaṃtrāsān agner darśanalālasān jalecaraḥ klāntamanās tejasāgneḥ pradīpitaḥ uvāca devān maṇḍūko rasātalatalotthitaḥ
english: Then to those who were stricken with terror and yearning for the sight of Agni, a frog, a water-dweller, weary in spirit and scorched by the radiance of Agni, rose up from the depths of the nether region and spoke to the gods:

sanskrit: rasātalatale devā vasaty agnir iti prabho saṃtāpād iha saṃprāptaḥ pāvakaprabhavād aham
english: "In the depths of the nether region, O gods, dwells Agni, O lord; I have come here driven by the burning that springs from Pāvaka.

sanskrit: sa saṃsupto jale devā bhagavān havyavāhanaḥ apaḥ saṃsṛjya tejobhis tena saṃtāpitā vayam
english: He, the blessed Havyavāhana, lies asleep in the water, O gods; mingling the waters with his radiance, he has scorched us by it.

sanskrit: tasya darśanam iṣṭaṃ vo yadi devā vibhāvasoḥ tatrainam abhigacchadhvaṃ kāryaṃ vo yadi vahninā
english: If the sight of him, of Vibhāvasu, is your wish, O gods, go to him there, if you have business with Vahni.

sanskrit: gamyatāṃ sādhayiṣyāmo vayaṃ hy agnibhayāt surāḥ etāvad uktvā maṇḍūkas tvarito jalam āviśat
english: Let it be gone to; as for us, we shall make our escape from the fear of Agni, O gods." Having said only this, the frog hastily entered the water.

sanskrit: hutāśanas tu bubudhe maṇḍūkasyātha paiśunam śaśāpa sa tam āsādya na rasān vetsyasīti vai
english: But Hutāśana perceived the frog's treachery, and, coming upon him, cursed him: "You shall know no flavors."

sanskrit: taṃ sa saṃyujya śāpena maṇḍūkaṃ pāvako yayau anyatra vāsāya vibhur na ca devān adarśayat
english: Having bound the frog with that curse, the all-pervading Pāvaka went elsewhere to dwell, and did not show himself to the gods.

sanskrit: devās tv anugrahaṃ cakrur maṇḍūkānāṃ bhṛgūdvaha yat tac chṛṇu mahābāho gadato mama sarvaśaḥ
english: But the gods bestowed a favor upon the frogs, O scion of Bhṛgu; hear it all from me as I tell it, O mighty-armed one.

sanskrit: devā ūcuḥ agniśāpād ajihvāpi rasajñānabahiṣkṛtāḥ sarasvatīṃ bahuvidhāṃ yūyam uccārayiṣyatha
english: The gods said: "Though tongueless and cut off from the knowledge of flavors by Agni's curse, you shall utter speech of many kinds.

sanskrit: bilavāsagatāṃś caiva nirādānān acetasaḥ gatāsūn api vaḥ śuṣkān bhūmiḥ saṃdhārayiṣyati tamogatāyām api ca niśāyāṃ vicariṣyatha
english: Even when you dwell in holes, foodless and senseless, even when lifeless and dried up, the earth shall sustain you; and you shall roam abroad even in the darkness-shrouded night."

sanskrit: ity uktvā tāṃs tato devāḥ punar eva mahīm imām parīyur jvalanasyārthe na cāvindan hutāśanam
english: Having spoken thus to them, the gods then ranged once more over this earth for the sake of the Burning One, yet they did not find Hutāśana.

sanskrit: atha tān dviradaḥ kaś cit surendradviradopamaḥ aśvatthastho 'gnir ity evaṃ prāha devān bhṛgūdvaha
english: Then a certain elephant, like unto the elephant of the king of the gods, said this to them, O scion of Bhṛgu: "Agni dwells within the aśvattha tree."

sanskrit: śaśāpa jvalanaḥ sarvān dviradān krodhamūrchitaḥ pratīpā bhavatāṃ jihvā bhavitrīti bhṛgūdvaha
english: The Burning One, overcome with wrath, cursed all the elephants: "Your tongue shall be turned backward," O scion of Bhṛgu.

sanskrit: ity uktvā niḥsṛto 'śvatthād agnir vāraṇasūcitaḥ praviveśa śamīgarbham atha vahniḥ suṣupsayā
english: Having said this, Agni, betrayed by the elephant, came forth from the aśvattha; then Vahni entered the womb of the śamī tree, desiring to sleep.

sanskrit: anugrahaṃ tu nāgānāṃ yaṃ cakruḥ śṛṇu taṃ prabho devā bhṛgukulaśreṣṭha prītāḥ satyaparākramāḥ
english: Hear now the favor that the gods, whose valor is truth, bestowed, well pleased, upon the elephants, O lord, O best of Bhṛgu's line.

sanskrit: devā ūcuḥ pratīpayā jihvayāpi sarvāhārān kariṣyatha vācaṃ coccārayiṣyadhvam uccair avyañjitākṣaram ity uktvā punar evāgnim anusasrur divaukasaḥ
english: The gods said: "Even with your backward-turned tongue you shall take all your food, and you shall utter a voice aloud, with unarticulated sound." Having said this, the dwellers of heaven once more went in pursuit of Agni.

sanskrit: aśvatthān niḥsṛtaś cāgniḥ śamīgarbhagatas tadā śukena khyāpito vipra taṃ devāḥ samupādravan
english: And Agni, having come forth from the aśvattha, had then entered the womb of the śamī; betrayed by a parrot, O brāhmaṇa, the gods rushed upon him.

sanskrit: śaśāpa śukam agnis tu vāgvihīno bhaviṣyasi jihvāṃ cāvartayām āsa tasyāpi hutabhuk tadā
english: But Agni cursed the parrot: "You shall be bereft of speech"; and the eater of oblations then turned that one's tongue backward too.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā tu jvalanaṃ devāḥ śukam ūcur dayānvitāḥ bhavitā na tvam atyantaṃ śakune naṣṭavāg iti
english: But the gods, seeing the Burning One, spoke to the parrot, filled with compassion: "You shall not, O bird, be wholly deprived of speech.

sanskrit: āvṛttajihvasya sato vākyaṃ kāntaṃ bhaviṣyati bālasyeva pravṛddhasya kalam avyaktam adbhutam
english: Though your tongue is turned backward, your speech shall be lovely—soft, indistinct, and wondrous, like that of a grown person who yet speaks as a child."

sanskrit: ity uktvā taṃ śamīgarbhe vahnim ālakṣya devatāḥ tad evāyatanaṃ cakruḥ puṇyaṃ sarvakriyāsv api
english: Having said this, and beholding Vahni within the womb of the śamī, the gods made that very tree his holy abode for all sacred rites.

sanskrit: tataḥprabhṛti cāpy agniḥ śamīgarbheṣu dṛśyate utpādane tathopāyam anujagmuś ca mānavāḥ
english: From that time forth Agni is found within the wombs of the śamī, and men too followed this means for the kindling of fire.

sanskrit: āpo rasātale yās tu saṃsṛṣṭāś citrabhānunā tāḥ parvataprasravaṇair ūṣmāṃ muñcanti bhārgava pāvakenādhiśayatā saṃtaptās tasya tejasā
english: Those waters in the nether region that were mingled with Citrabhānu, O Bhārgava, release their heat through the springs of the mountains, scorched as they were by the radiance of Pāvaka, who lay couched within them.

sanskrit: tato 'gnir devatā dṛṣṭvā babhūva vyathitas tadā kim āgamanam ity evaṃ tān apṛcchata pāvakaḥ
english: Then Agni, seeing the gods, became troubled, and Pāvaka asked them thus: "What is the purpose of your coming?"

sanskrit: tam ūcur vibudhāḥ sarve te caiva paramarṣayaḥ tvāṃ niyokṣyāmahe kārye tad bhavān kartum arhati kṛte ca tasmin bhavitā tavāpi sumahān guṇaḥ
english: All the wise ones and those supreme sages said to him: "We would appoint you to a task; you ought to perform it; and when it is done, a great benefit shall accrue to you as well."

sanskrit: agnir uvāca brūta yad bhavatāṃ kāryaṃ sarvaṃ kartāsmi tat surāḥ bhavatāṃ hi niyojyo 'haṃ mā vo 'trāstu vicāraṇā
english: Agni said: "Tell me what your task is; I shall do it all, O gods; for I am yours to command—let there be no hesitation in you over this."

sanskrit: devā ūcuḥ asuras tārako nāma brahmaṇo varadarpitaḥ asmān prabādhate vīryād vadhas tasya vidhīyatām
english: The gods said: "An asura named Tāraka, made proud by Brahmā's boon, oppresses us by his might; let his slaying be ordained.

sanskrit: imān devagaṇāṃs tāta prajāpatigaṇāṃs tathā ṛṣīṃś cāpi mahābhāgān paritrāyasva pāvaka
english: Save these hosts of gods, dear one, and the hosts of the Prajāpatis, and the greatly blessed sages too, O Pāvaka.

sanskrit: apatyaṃ tejasā yuktaṃ pravīraṃ janaya prabho yad bhayaṃ no 'surāt tasmān nāśayed dhavyavāhana
english: Beget an offspring endowed with radiance, a great hero, O lord, who shall destroy the fear we have from that asura, O Havyavāhana.

sanskrit: śaptānāṃ no mahādevyā nānyad asti parāyaṇam anyatra bhavato vīryaṃ tasmāt trāyasva nas tataḥ
english: For us, cursed by the great Goddess, there is no other refuge than your valor; therefore deliver us from this peril."

sanskrit: ity uktaḥ sa tathety uktvā bhagavān havyakavyabhuk jagāmātha durādharṣo gaṅgāṃ bhāgīrathīṃ prati
english: Thus addressed, the blessed bearer of oblations to gods and ancestors said "So be it," and that one hard to assail went then toward the Gaṅgā, the daughter of Bhagīratha.

sanskrit: tayā cāpy abhavan miśro garbhaś cāsyābhavat tadā vavṛdhe sa tadā garbhaḥ kakṣe kṛṣṇagatir yathā
english: He mingled with her, and an embryo formed within her then; and that embryo grew, as the fire whose path is black grows in dry brushwood.

sanskrit: tejasā tasya garbhasya gaṅgā vihvalacetanā saṃtāpam agamat tīvraṃ sā soḍhuṃ na śaśāka ha
english: By the radiance of that embryo Gaṅgā, her senses overwhelmed, came to a fierce burning, and she could not endure it.

sanskrit: āhite jvalanenātha garbhe tejaḥsamanvite gaṅgāyām asuraḥ kaś cid bhairavaṃ nādam utsṛjat
english: When the embryo, charged with radiance, had been placed by the Burning One in Gaṅgā, a certain asura let loose a terrible roar.

sanskrit: abuddhāpatitenātha nādena vipulena sā vitrastodbhrāntanayanā gaṅgā viplutalocanā visaṃjñā nāśakad garbhaṃ saṃdhārayitum ātmanā
english: At that vast roar, fallen upon her unawares, Gaṅgā—her eyes wide with terror and rolling, her gaze swimming, her senses gone—was unable to hold the embryo within herself.

sanskrit: sā tu tejaḥparītāṅgī kampamānā ca jāhnavī uvāca vacanaṃ vipra tadā garbhabaloddhatā na te śaktāsmi bhagavaṃs tejaso 'sya vidhāraṇe
english: Then Jāhnavī, her limbs encompassed by radiance and trembling, overborne by the embryo, spoke these words, O brāhmaṇa: "I am not able, O blessed one, to bear up this radiance of yours.

sanskrit: vimūḍhāsmi kṛtānena tathāsvāsthyaṃ kṛtaṃ param vihvalā cāsmi bhagavaṃs tejo naṣṭaṃ ca me 'nagha
english: I am bewildered, and by it I have been made most ill at ease; I am overwhelmed, O blessed one, and my own radiance is lost, O sinless one.

sanskrit: dhāraṇe nāsya śaktāhaṃ garbhasya tapatāṃ vara utsrakṣye 'ham imaṃ duḥkhān na tu kāmāt kathaṃ cana
english: I am not able to hold this embryo, O best of those that burn; I shall release it out of distress, and in no wise out of any wish to do so.

sanskrit: na cetaso 'sti saṃsparśo mama deva vibhāvaso āpadarthe hi saṃbandhaḥ susūkṣmo 'pi mahādyute
english: There is no touch of inclination in my heart, O god Vibhāvasu; for a bond formed in time of distress, even the subtlest, is no true bond, O greatly resplendent one.

sanskrit: yad atra guṇasaṃpannam itaraṃ vā hutāśana tvayy eva tad ahaṃ manye dharmādharmau ca kevalau
english: Whatever here is endowed with merit, or otherwise, O Hutāśana, I deem that to rest in you alone, and the merit and demerit of it to be wholly yours."

sanskrit: tām uvāca tato vahnir dhāryatāṃ dhāryatām ayam garbho mattejasā yukto mahāguṇaphalodayaḥ
english: Then Vahni said to her: "Let it be borne, let this embryo be borne, charged with my radiance, the source of great and meritorious fruit.

sanskrit: śaktā hy asi mahīṃ kṛtsnāṃ voḍhuṃ dhārayituṃ tathā na hi te kiṃ cid aprāpyaṃ madretodhāraṇād ṛte
english: For you are able to bear and to sustain the whole earth; there is nothing beyond your power, save the holding of my seed."

sanskrit: sā vahninā vāryamāṇā devaiś cāpi saridvarā samutsasarja taṃ garbhaṃ merau girivare tadā
english: Though held back by Vahni and by the gods, that best of rivers then cast off the embryo upon Meru, the noblest of mountains.

sanskrit: samarthā dhāraṇe cāpi rudratejaḥpradharṣitā nāśakat taṃ tadā garbhaṃ saṃdhārayitum ojasā
english: Though capable of bearing it, overborne by the radiance of Rudra, she was then unable to sustain that embryo by her strength.

sanskrit: sā samutsṛjya taṃ duḥkhād dīptavaiśvānaraprabham darśayām āsa cāgnis tāṃ tadā gaṅgāṃ bhṛgūdvaha papraccha saritāṃ śreṣṭhāṃ kaccid garbhaḥ sukhodayaḥ
english: Having cast off in distress that embryo, bright as the blazing Vaiśvānara, Agni then showed himself to Gaṅgā, O scion of Bhṛgu, and asked that best of rivers: "Is the embryo a happy birth?

sanskrit: kīdṛgvarṇo 'pi vā devi kīdṛgrūpaś ca dṛśyate tejasā kena vā yuktaḥ sarvam etad bravīhi me
english: Of what hue, O goddess, and of what form does it appear? And with what radiance is it endowed? Tell me all of this."

sanskrit: gaṅgovāca jātarūpaḥ sa garbho vai tejasā tvam ivānala suvarṇo vimalo dīptaḥ parvataṃ cāvabhāsayat
english: Gaṅgā said: "That embryo is of golden form, in radiance like to yourself, O Anala—of fair gold, spotless, blazing; and it lit up the mountain.

sanskrit: padmotpalavimiśrāṇāṃ hradānām iva śītalaḥ gandho 'sya sa kadambānāṃ tulyo vai tapatāṃ vara
english: It is cool as pools intermingled with lotuses and blue water-lilies; and its fragrance is equal to that of the kadamba blossoms, O best of those that burn.

sanskrit: tejasā tasya garbhasya bhāskarasyeva raśmibhiḥ yad dravyaṃ parisaṃsṛṣṭaṃ pṛthivyāṃ parvateṣu vā tat sarvaṃ kāñcanībhūtaṃ samantāt pratyadṛśyata
english: By the radiance of that embryo, as by the rays of the sun-maker, whatever substance was touched, upon the earth or in the mountains, all of that was seen on every side to have turned to gold.
